claims.statement: Folding decisions for β-hairpin structures are localized in the early blocks of ESMFold's 48-block folding trunk, and the sequence representation s is the active locus of that decision during this early window. Specifically, activation-patching s within an early window causes a significant drop (Δ hairpin rate ≥ 0.2 pp) in DSSP-based β-hairpin formation of the target region, while late-window s-patching or same-window z-patching produces a significantly smaller effect.

data.subset_note: cost-aware subsetting; 197 paired chains after strict alignment filters — well-powered for the observed Δ=-0.862 effect.

models: ESMFold (ESM-2 backbone + 48-block folding trunk + structure module)
claims.method: block-wise s-patching across 8 bands ({b_0_3, b_4_7, b_8_11, b_12_15, b_16_23, b_24_31, b_32_39, b_40_47}) with donor covers; three specificity controls run in-window: z-patching (same window), matched-mask s-patching (non-target residues), late-window s-patching. DSSP judge on ESMFold-predicted structure = ground truth. Family = Causal Attribution / Patching.

main_experiment.key_stats: early band b_0_3 (blocks 0-3): s-patch Δ=-0.862 (p=2.25e-36, N=197); z-patch same-window Δ=-0.011 (1.3% of s-patch); matched-ctrl Δ=-0.067 (7.7%); late-window (b_32_39) s-patch Δ=-0.085 (9.8%). All 5 predicates PASS.
main_experiment.headline: β-hairpin decision is strongly localized to early blocks 0-3, with s the active locus: s-patching in b_0_3 collapses hairpin rate from 100% to 13.8% while all three matched-specificity controls change hairpin rate by ≤10%.

claims.statement: In the early blocks, the seq2pair operation is the critical causal channel that transfers the β-hairpin folding decision from the sequence representation s into the pairwise representation z. Ablating seq2pair (donor-patch or zero-ablation) in the early window causes a significant drop in target β-hairpin formation, while a matched pair2seq intervention produces a significantly smaller effect (paired McNemar p < 0.05).

claims.statement: Charge is a linearly encoded chemical feature in early blocks of ESMFold's s representation (3-class balanced accuracy ≥ 0.75, permutation p < 0.001), and this charge feature exerts a causal effect on β-hairpin formation: opposite-charge steering on facing β-strands favors pairing (hairpin rate up, cross-strand distance down); same-charge steering suppresses pairing (hairpin rate down, cross-strand distance up). Dose-response |Spearman ρ| ≥ 0.7 with matched-control specificity.

data.source: PISCES-filtered set; M3a heldout_probe 40 chains + M3b 200 main + 50 calib for σ_proj
data.used_n: 40 chains for M3a probe + 179-N chains for M3b steering
data.subset_note: M3a heldout_probe under-scale (40 vs planned 250) tagged as suspected_under_power — but verdict still definitive (bacc=1.0, p<0.001).

claims.method: M3a — linear 3-class charge probe on s[block_k, :, :] for k∈{0,2,4,6}, 1000-permutation null → extract v_charge from best block's probe (positive-class minus negative-class weight vector, L2-normalized). M3b — additive steering s[block_k, res, :] += β · σ_proj · v_charge (rebound from raw α to β · σ_proj units per steering-coefficient-tuning tip; σ_proj at block 0 ≈ 21.55) on cross-strand pair in {same, opposite} configurations, β ∈ {-3, -1, 0, +1, +3}; DSSP eval + matched-control non-target pair + random-direction control.

main_experiment.verdict: partial [M3a supported; M3b real null — 'linearly encoded but not causally used' educational middle result]
main_experiment.key_stats: M3a: best block=0, balanced accuracy=1.0 (all 4 sampled blocks bacc=1.0), permutation p<0.001, PASS all predicates. M3b: same-vs-opposite Δ=-0.006 at β=+3σ (p=1.0000, N=179); FAIL 5 causal predicates; PASS random_ctrl_near_baseline. 175/179 chains had hairpin=1 across the entire β sweep.
main_experiment.headline: Charge is trivially decodable (bacc=1.0) in every early block but additive steering along v_charge does NOT flip hairpin outcomes — a genuine 'linearly encoded but not causally used' result: decodability ≠ causal sufficiency. Consistent with the concept-erasure and truth-direction literature (Belrose 2023, Marks & Tegmark 2023).

claims.final_status: ⚪ integrity_only (Stage 1 audit passed; swap-test deferred — max_verify_claims_cap; C1 picked over C3 by importance) — partial main experiment (M3a supported; M3b real null)
caveats: M3a heldout_probe scale (40 vs planned 250 chains) [suspected under-power: used_n 40/250, seeds 1/1, grid 4/4] — but bacc=1.0 with permutation p<0.001 leaves the M3a verdict definitive despite tag.

M3b null could reflect: (a) charge is correlated but not causal for hairpin; (b) block-0 charge direction is washed out by downstream recycle/normalization; (c) hairpin decision uses non-linear combinations that additive steering cannot reach. The educational middle result was explicitly anticipated in the plan.

figures.caption: M3a — 3-class charge probe balanced-accuracy + AUROC by early block; all 4 sampled blocks (0, 2, 4, 6) achieve bacc=1.0 and AUROC=1.0 with permutation p<0.001. Chance = 1/3 (dotted line).

C3b two-panel: (a) target-region hairpin rate stays flat ≈0.99 across β ∈ {-3,-1,0,+1,+3}·σ_proj for both same and opposite configurations — a real null (175/179 chains hairpin=1 throughout the sweep); (b) mean ΔpLDDT vs β confirms the perturbation itself is non-zero, so the null in (a) is NOT a no-op — steering along v_charge does perturb the residual stream but does not deflect downstream folding decisions. Illustrates decodability ≠ causal sufficiency.
